_doc: N-LAGLADDER curve spec — RR-EMIT's first PRODUCTION authoring run (the nit
spec beside it was a lossless re-encoding of shipped content; this one
authors new content). NOT loaded at runtime: app/domain/personas.py globs
content/personas/*.json non-recursively, so this subdirectory is invisible
to the pack loader. It is read only by backend/tools/rr_emit.py, which
emits the `unopened` nodes of the file named in `emits`.
PROVENANCE OF THE IDENTITY TARGET, stated ONCE here so the tests can point
at it instead of repeating a bare number: §5 LAG VPIP 21-27 / PFR 17-23
(9-max full ring, online micro-low NL cash, ledger #14 full-ring-specialist
source; confidence MEDIUM, band edges DIRECTIONAL). Nothing in this slice
gates on those edges — they are the reason the shape moved, not a target
the content was fitted to.
WHAT THIS REPAIRS (theory-HIGH finding T-H1, wave-2 ledger): the lag's
first-in ladder carried its width in DOMINATED OFFSUIT hands, worst in
early seats — at UTG it raised 12.49% of all combos offsuit against only
7.90% suited, i.e. HALF the opening range was offsuit and the lag opened
MORE offsuit than the tag from every early seat. That surplus is what
later arrives at `vs_3bet` as call mass the persona cannot defend.
THE FIX IS A COMPOSITION SWAP AT CONSTANT WIDTH, NOT A TRIM. Offsuit width
falls at every seat (UTG 12.49 -> 8.69, UTG2 17.38 -> 12.31, HJ 26.61 ->
22.62) and suited width rises at every seat (UTG 7.90 -> 10.50, UTG2 10.92
-> 15.51, HJ 15.20 -> 19.13), while the combo-weighted TOTAL stays within
0.36pp of the pre-slice ladder at every seat (seat-average 43.15 -> 43.04).
WHY THE TOTAL DID NOT COME DOWN — measured, not assumed (review fold, fix
1). The first cut of this slice tightened the seat-average to 39.22 and
drove measured population PFR to 15.77, UNDER the §5 floor of 17. A 10-seed
sweep of metric #3 at n=2000 then showed the pre-slice pack itself sits at
PFR 17.32 +- 0.34 — i.e. ON the floor, with no headroom to spend. Any real
width reduction therefore breaches §5, so the width was restored and the
whole deliverable is the composition. This ladder re-measures at PFR 17.32
+- 0.30, identical to pre-slice.
N-LAGCOMP2 (2026-07-31, lag.json 1.4.0) — SECOND composition swap, LATE
SEATS ONLY (CO / BTN / SB). N-LAGLADDER above fixed the EARLY seats and
left the late ones nearly alone (CO offsuit moved -0.90, BTN -0.36), so
after N-TAGCOMP fixed the tag's shape the lag ended up opening a wider
TOTAL range than the tag while covering LESS of the suited universe from
exactly the seats where suited hands are worth the most:
suited %, lag vs tag   CO 17.01 vs 19.00 · BTN 19.91 vs 22.47 ·
A wider range that is a SUBSET in suited is the same defect T-M2 and
N-TAGCOMP condemned; the lag's surplus was sitting in offsuit junk.
The repair is again a swap, and here it is EXACTLY width-neutral — the
combo-weighted total at all three seats is unchanged to the last combo
(CO 704.4, BTN 874.8, SB 687.6 of 1326), because the lag's measured PFR
sits ON the §5 floor (see the paragraph above) and there is nothing to
spend. Per seat, suited -> offsuit, in percent of all 1326 combos:
CO   suited 17.01 -> 20.63   offsuit 30.23 -> 26.61   total 53.12
BTN  suited 19.91 -> 23.53   offsuit 40.18 -> 36.56   total 65.97
SB   suited 17.01 -> 19.73   offsuit 28.96 -> 26.24   total 51.86
Pairs are untouched (13 at every one of these seats, 5.88%), as in
N-TAGCOMP: moving the pair band too would confound the measurement.
The suited side is now a SUPERSET of the tag's at all three seats — every
suited class the tag opens, the lag opens, at equal or greater weight
(BTN is the whole suited universe at weight 1.0, which is what a 66% open
means). The offsuit side stays ABOVE the tag's at every seat, so the
N-LAGLADDER preservation gate is untouched and still green.
The offsuit mass came off the WEAK-KICKER BOTTOM of the low rows (CO Qo
Q7o->Q8o core, Jo J7o->J8o, To T7o->T8o, 9o out of the core; BTN Jo
J5o->J6o, To T6o->T7o, 9o 97o->98o, 8o out of the core; SB the same three
rows as CO), never off the aces or kings, and the authoring rule below
still holds at each of the three seats.
AUTHORING RULE used for the offsuit rows (not enforced by the emitter, and
deliberately not gated — an authoring habit, not a law): the weakest kicker
played at full weight must not get STRONGER as the high card gets weaker,
so a row never plays K8o at the fringe weight while Q8o sits in the core.
Suited rows are exempt: 65s outranks 95s on connectedness, so the
same-kicker comparison is not a domination relation there.
`depths[row]` = how many classes down that row the CORE tier plays, with
rows ordered strongest-kicker-first (As = AKs, AQs, ...). Rows absent from
`depths` are not played at all; a row present with depth 0 is played by the
slope tier only (the curve's leading edge spilling into a fresh row).
`slopes[row]` overrides the slope tier width for one row (one width per
slope tier); the lag uses `[0]` to stop a row cleanly at its core.
`raise_pct` is an ASSERTED ANNOTATION, never an emitter input: the combo-
weighted raise width the emitted node actually produces, cross-checked by
test_rr_emit.py. Floors are authored; they are never fitted to a target.
There is deliberately nowhere in this file to put a percentile or width
parameter (range-representation-design.md sec.1).
